doc.brief: Can be applied to text contained in a `GtkTextBuffer`.
doc.md:
Can be applied to text contained in a `GtkTextBuffer`.

You may wish to begin by reading the
[text widget conceptual overview](section-text-widget.html),
which gives an overview of all the objects and data types
related to the text widget and how they work together.

Tags should be in the [`TextTagTable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextTagTable) for a given
`GtkTextBuffer` before using them with that buffer.

[`TextBuffer.create_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:create_tag) is the best way to create tags.
See “gtk4-demo” for numerous examples.

For each property of `GtkTextTag`, there is a “set” property, e.g.
“font-set” corresponds to “font”. These “set” properties reflect
whether a property has been set or not.

They are maintained by GTK and you should not set them independently.

changed.brief: Emits the [`TextTagTable::tag-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextTagTable#event:tag-changed) signal on the `GtkTextTagTable` where the tag is included.
changed.md:
Emits the [`TextTagTable::tag-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextTagTable#event:tag-changed) signal on the
`GtkTextTagTable` where the tag is included.

The signal is already emitted when setting a `GtkTextTag` property.
This function is useful for a `GtkTextTag` subclass.

set_priority.md:
Sets the priority of a `GtkTextTag`.

Valid priorities start at 0 and go to one less than
[`TextTagTable.get_size()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextTagTable#method:get_size). Each tag in a table
has a unique priority; setting the priority of one tag shifts
the priorities of all the other tags in the table to maintain
a unique priority for each tag.

Higher priority tags “win” if two tags both set the same text
attribute. When adding a tag to a tag table, it will be assigned
the highest priority in the table by default; so normally the
precedence of a set of tags is the order in which they were added
to the table, or created with [`TextBuffer.create_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:create_tag),
which adds the tag to the buffer’s table automatically.

accumulative-margin.brief: Whether the margins accumulate or override each other.
accumulative-margin.md:
Whether the margins accumulate or override each other.

When set to `TRUE` the margins of this tag are added to the margins
of any other non-accumulative margins present. When set to `FALSE`
the margins override one another (the default).

background-full-height.brief: Whether the background color fills the entire line height or only the height of the tagged characters.
background-full-height.md:
Whether the background color fills the entire line height
or only the height of the tagged characters.

direction.brief: Text direction, e.g. right-to-left or left-to-right.
direction.md: Text direction, e.g. right-to-left or left-to-right.

editable.brief: Whether the text can be modified by the user.
editable.md: Whether the text can be modified by the user.

fallback.md:
Whether font fallback is enabled.

When set to `TRUE`, other fonts will be substituted
where the current font is missing glyphs.

family.brief: Name of the font family, e.g.
family.md: Name of the font family, e.g. Sans, Helvetica, Times, Monospace.

font.brief: Font description as string, e.g. \"Sans Italic 12\".
font.md:
Font description as string, e.g. \"Sans Italic 12\".

Note that the initial value of this property depends on
the internals of `PangoFontDescription`.

font-features.brief: OpenType font features, as a string.
font-features.md: OpenType font features, as a string.

indent.brief: Amount to indent the paragraph, in pixels.
indent.md:
Amount to indent the paragraph, in pixels.

A negative value of indent will produce a hanging indentation.
That is, the first line will have the full width, and subsequent
lines will be indented by the absolute value of indent.

insert-hyphens.brief: Whether to insert hyphens at breaks.
insert-hyphens.md: Whether to insert hyphens at breaks.

invisible.md:
Whether this text is hidden.

Note that there may still be problems with the support for invisible
text, in particular when navigating programmatically inside a buffer
containing invisible segments.

language.brief: The language this text is in, as an ISO code.
language.md:
The language this text is in, as an ISO code.

Pango can use this as a hint when rendering the text.
If not set, an appropriate default will be used.

Note that the initial value of this property depends
on the current locale, see also `get_default_language`.

left-margin.brief: Width of the left margin in pixels.
left-margin.md: Width of the left margin in pixels.

letter-spacing.brief: Extra spacing between graphemes, in Pango units.
letter-spacing.md: Extra spacing between graphemes, in Pango units.

line-height.brief: Factor to scale line height by.
line-height.md: Factor to scale line height by.

name.brief: The name used to refer to the tag.
name.md:
The name used to refer to the tag.

`NULL` for anonymous tags.

overline.brief: Style of overline for this text.
overline.md: Style of overline for this text.

overline-rgba.brief: This property modifies the color of overlines.
overline-rgba.md:
This property modifies the color of overlines.

If not set, overlines will use the foreground color.

paragraph-background.brief: The paragraph background color as a string.
paragraph-background.md: The paragraph background color as a string.

paragraph-background-rgba.brief: The paragraph background color as a `GdkRGBA`.
paragraph-background-rgba.md: The paragraph background color as a `GdkRGBA`.

pixels-above-lines.brief: Pixels of blank space above paragraphs.
pixels-above-lines.md: Pixels of blank space above paragraphs.

pixels-below-lines.brief: Pixels of blank space below paragraphs.
pixels-below-lines.md: Pixels of blank space below paragraphs.

pixels-inside-wrap.brief: Pixels of blank space between wrapped lines in a paragraph.
pixels-inside-wrap.md: Pixels of blank space between wrapped lines in a paragraph.

right-margin.brief: Width of the right margin, in pixels.
right-margin.md: Width of the right margin, in pixels.

rise.brief: Offset of text above the baseline, in Pango units.
rise.md:
Offset of text above the baseline, in Pango units.

Negative values go below the baseline.

scale.brief: Font size as a scale factor relative to the default font size.
scale.md:
Font size as a scale factor relative to the default font size.

This properly adapts to theme changes, etc. so is recommended.
Pango predefines some scales such as %PANGO_SCALE_X_LARGE.

sentence.brief: Whether this tag represents a single sentence.
sentence.md:
Whether this tag represents a single sentence.

This affects cursor movement.

strikethrough.brief: Whether to strike through the text.
strikethrough.md: Whether to strike through the text.

strikethrough-rgba.brief: This property modifies the color of strikeouts.
strikethrough-rgba.md:
This property modifies the color of strikeouts.

If not set, strikeouts will use the foreground color.

strikethrough-rgba-set.brief: If the `strikethrough-rgba` property has been set.
strikethrough-rgba-set.md: If the `strikethrough-rgba` property has been set.

text-transform.brief: How to transform the text for display.
text-transform.md: How to transform the text for display.

underline.brief: Style of underline for this text.
underline.md: Style of underline for this text.

underline-rgba.brief: This property modifies the color of underlines.
underline-rgba.md:
This property modifies the color of underlines.

If not set, underlines will use the foreground color.

If [`TextTag:underline`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextTag#property:underline) is set to %PANGO_UNDERLINE_ERROR,
an alternate color may be applied instead of the foreground. Setting
this property will always override those defaults.

underline-rgba-set.brief: If the `underline-rgba` property has been set.
underline-rgba-set.md: If the `underline-rgba` property has been set.

word.brief: Whether this tag represents a single word.
word.md:
Whether this tag represents a single word.

This affects line breaks and cursor movement.

wrap-mode.brief: Whether to wrap lines never, at word boundaries, or at character boundaries.
wrap-mode.md:
Whether to wrap lines never, at word boundaries, or
at character boundaries.
